py: wǒ zhōu mò zài gōng yuán pǎo bù
en: I go running in the park at weekends.
why: Time comes first, then 在 + place, then the verb. 在公园 cannot trail 跑步 the way English "in the park" does.

zh: 他们春节在老家包饺子。
py: tā men chūn jié zài lǎo jiā bāo jiǎo zi
en: They make dumplings back in their hometown at Spring Festival.
why: Both the time word 春节 and the place phrase 在老家 sit before 包饺子, time first. Putting them after the verb copies English order.

zh: 我们中秋节晚上在院子里吃月饼。
py: wǒ men zhōng qiū jié wǎn shang zài yuàn zi lǐ chī yuè bǐng
en: We eat mooncakes in the courtyard on the evening of the Mid-Autumn Festival.
why: Subject, time, place, verb phrase. The time may also open the sentence, but it can never follow 吃月饼.

zh: 孩子们星期六下午在游泳馆学游泳。
py: hái zi men xīng qī liù xià wǔ zài yóu yǒng guǎn xué yóu yǒng
en: The children learn to swim at the pool on Saturday afternoons.
why: The scene (when, then where) is set before the verb 学. 在游泳馆 after 学游泳 would be English order.

zh: 我弟弟明年夏天要在海边参加游泳比赛。
py: wǒ dì di míng nián xià tiān yào zài hǎi biān cān jiā yóu yǒng bǐ sài
en: My younger brother will take part in a swimming competition at the seaside next summer.
why: The modal 要 comes before 在海边, and the time word sits next to the subject. The place phrase stays ahead of 参加.

zh: 元宵节我们在公园看灯。
py: yuán xiāo jié wǒ men zài gōng yuán kàn dēng
en: On the Lantern Festival we go and look at the lanterns in the park.
why: The festival is a time word, so it goes before the verb, either ahead of the subject or right after it; 在公园 follows it.

zh: 我星期六跟朋友一起打篮球。
py: wǒ xīng qī liù gēn péng you yī qǐ dǎ lán qiú
en: I play basketball with friends on Saturdays.
why: 跟朋友一起 says who you do it with and goes before the verb, after the time word. "打篮球跟朋友一起" is English order.

py: wǒ men míng tiān yī qǐ qù pá shān
en: We are going hiking together tomorrow.
why: After a plural subject, 一起 goes directly before the verb phrase 去爬山. It cannot follow 去 or end the sentence.

zh: 她想跟姐姐一起去滑雪。
py: tā xiǎng gēn jiě jie yī qǐ qù huá xuě
en: She wants to go skiing with her older sister.
why: The modal 想 comes before the whole 跟姐姐一起 frame, which in turn comes before the main verb 去滑雪.

zh: 过年时我们总是和家人一起看春节晚会。
py: guò nián shí wǒ men zǒng shì hé jiā rén yī qǐ kàn chūn jié wǎn huì
en: At New Year we always watch the Spring Festival Gala with our family.
why: Order: time, subject, adverb 总是, companion frame, verb. The adverb comes before 和家人一起, not after it.

py: wǒ men yī qǐ tī zú qiú ba
en: Let us play football together.
why: 一起 goes right before the verb phrase. 我们踢足球一起 would copy English "together" at the end.

zh: 我明天想跟老同学一起去看龙舟比赛。
py: wǒ míng tiān xiǎng gēn lǎo tóng xué yī qǐ qù kàn lóng zhōu bǐ sài
en: Tomorrow I want to go and watch the dragon boat race with an old classmate.
why: The companion frame belongs right before 去看, after 想. The time word may sit before the subject or on either side of 想, but never after the verb.

py: wǒ zuò dì tiě qù tǐ yù guǎn
en: I take the subway to the stadium.
why: The means of travel 坐地铁 comes before the main verb 去. "我去体育馆坐地铁" would say you go there and then ride.

zh: 他每天骑自行车去公园。
py: tā měi tiān qí zì xíng chē qù gōng yuán
en: He cycles to the park every day.
why: Time, then means (骑自行车), then the main verb 去. The means is never placed after 去公园.

zh: 爸爸用手机拍了很多照片。
py: bà ba yòng shǒu jī pāi le hěn duō zhào piàn
en: Dad took lots of photos with his phone.
why: The tool 用手机 comes before the verb 拍. English puts "with his phone" at the end; Chinese does not.

zh: 妈妈用新买的锅煮饺子。
py: mā ma yòng xīn mǎi de guō zhǔ jiǎo zi
en: Mum cooks the dumplings in the newly bought pot.
why: The instrument phrase 用…锅 goes before 煮饺子. Inside it, the clause 新买的 sits before 锅.

py: tā màn màn de dǎ kāi le hóng bāo
en: He slowly opened the red envelope.
why: A manner adverb with 地 goes before the verb it describes. 他打开了红包慢慢地 is English order and wrong.

zh: 春节时很多人坐高铁回老家。
py: chūn jié shí hěn duō rén zuò gāo tiě huí lǎo jiā
en: At Spring Festival many people go back to their hometowns by high-speed train.
why: Time and means both come before 回老家. 坐高铁 is a verb phrase placed ahead of the main verb, and the time word may open the sentence or follow 很多人.

py: wǒ yě xǐ huan yóu yǒng
en: I like swimming too.
why: 也 goes after the subject and before the verb. English "too" at the end does not carry over.

py: tā jiǔ diǎn cái dào tǐ yù guǎn
en: He did not get to the stadium until nine.
why: 才 follows the time word and comes before the verb. It cannot come before 九点 or after 到体育馆.

py: bǐ sài bā diǎn jiù kāi shǐ le
en: The match started as early as eight.
why: 就 (earlier than expected) follows the time word and precedes the verb. The time word may also open the sentence.

py: wǒ men cháng cháng qù yóu yǒng
en: We often go swimming.
why: Frequency adverbs like 常常 sit between the subject and the verb, never at the end of the sentence.

py: tā yī zhí zài xué dǎ wǎng qiú
en: She has been learning to play tennis all along.
why: 一直 comes after the subject and before the verb phrase 在学打网球; it cannot start the sentence.

zh: 我今年也想参加马拉松。
py: wǒ jīn nián yě xiǎng cān jiā mǎ lā sōng
en: I want to run in a marathon this year too.
why: 也 comes after the time word and before the modal 想. The time word can also lead the sentence, but 也 never leads it.

py: tā men chūn jié dōu huí lǎo jiā
en: They all go back to their hometowns at Spring Festival.
why: 都 follows the subject and the time word and precedes the verb. Putting 都 before 春节 or after 回老家 is wrong.

py: wǒ men yě dōu xǐ huan tī zú qiú
en: We all like playing football too.
why: Stacked adverbs run 也 then 都 before the verb. 都也 reverses them.

py: tā men yě dōu bù huì huá bīng
en: None of them can skate either.
why: The fixed chain is 也, 都, 不. 不 sits last, next to the verb, and the meaning is "none", not "not all".

zh: 我们都没参加过马拉松。
py: wǒ men dōu méi cān jiā guo mǎ lā sōng
en: None of us has run in a marathon.
why: 都 comes before 没, matching the chain 都 then negation. 没都 would be wrong, and 都没 here means none.

py: wǒ yě bù xǐ huan pǎo bù
en: I do not like running either.
why: 也 comes before 不. 不也喜欢 reverses the order and is wrong.

py: wǒ men bù dōu shì qiú mí
en: Not all of us are sports fans.
why: 不 before 都 means "not all". The cue says some are fans and some are not, so 都不 (none) would change the meaning.

py: zhè shì nǎi nai bāo de jiǎo zi
en: These are the dumplings Grandma made.
why: The clause 奶奶包 plus 的 comes before the noun 饺子. Chinese has no "dumplings that Grandma made" order.

zh: 我喜欢爷爷送我的风筝。
py: wǒ xǐ huan yé ye sòng wǒ de fēng zheng
en: I like the kite Grandpa gave me.
why: The whole description 爷爷送我的 goes before 风筝. Nothing can follow the noun.

zh: 穿红衣服的人是我们的教练。
py: chuān hóng yī fu de rén shì wǒ men de jiào liàn
en: The person in red is our coach.
why: 穿红衣服的 describes 人 and stands in front of it. 人穿红衣服的 would copy English relative-clause order.

zh: 妈妈买了一件很漂亮的新衣服。
py: mā ma mǎi le yī jiàn hěn piào liang de xīn yī fu
en: Mum bought a very pretty new outfit.
why: Number and measure word come before the description, then the noun: 一件很漂亮的新衣服. The description cannot trail 衣服.

zh: 昨天参加比赛的同学都拿到了奖牌。
py: zuó tiān cān jiā bǐ sài de tóng xué dōu ná dào le jiǎng pái
en: The classmates who took part in yesterday's competition all won medals.
why: The time word 昨天 is inside the modifier clause in front of 同学. 都 then comes before the verb of the main clause.

zh: 我想看你在端午节拍的照片。
py: wǒ xiǎng kàn nǐ zài duān wǔ jié pāi de zhào piàn
en: I want to see the photos you took at Dragon Boat Festival.
why: The time phrase stays inside the clause 你在端午节拍, which sits before 照片. English "photos you took…" order is wrong here.

py: nǐ xiǎng wán shén me
en: What do you want to play?
why: The question word stays in the object slot where the answer would be, after the verb. 什么你想玩 is wrong.

py: nǐ shén me shí hou qù dǎ qiú
en: When are you going to play ball?
why: 什么时候 is a time word, so it goes before the verb, after the subject or ahead of it. It is not moved to the end like English "when".

zh: 你打算跟谁一起去滑冰？
py: nǐ dǎ suàn gēn shéi yī qǐ qù huá bīng
en: Who are you planning to go skating with?
why: 谁 stays inside the 跟…一起 frame, before the verb. English puts "who" first; Chinese does not.

py: nǐ zài nǎ r yóu yǒng
en: Where do you swim?
why: 哪儿 stays in the place slot, after 在 and before the verb. 你游泳在哪儿 would be English order.

py: nǐ men zěn me guò zhōng qiū jié
en: How do you celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival?
why: 怎么 is a manner word and goes before the verb 过. It cannot be fronted or put at the end.

py: zhè chǎng bǐ sài wǒ kàn guo
en: I have seen this match.
why: A known object may open the sentence as topic, with the rest in normal order. The plain order and the topic-after-subject order are also fine.

py: nà ge qiú pāi wǒ yě xiǎng mǎi
en: I want to buy that racket too.
why: With the topic fronted, 也 still follows the subject 我. 那个球拍也我想买 would be wrong.

zh: 这些粽子我已经吃完了。
py: zhè xiē zòng zi wǒ yǐ jīng chī wán le
en: I have already finished eating these rice dumplings.
why: 粽子 is definite (这些), so it can be the topic. 已经 stays after the subject, not before the topic.

py: zhōng guó xiàng qí wǒ yě huì xià
en: I can play Chinese chess too.
why: A general topic like 中国象棋 can come first. The adverb 也 then follows 我 and precedes 会.

zh: 今年的春节晚会我还没看。
py: jīn nián de chūn jié wǎn huì wǒ hái méi kàn
en: I have not watched this year's Spring Festival Gala yet.
why: The Gala is known to both speakers, so it can be topic. 还 stays right before 没 after the subject.

py: wǒ xiān chī fàn zài qù yóu yǒng
en: I will eat first and then go swimming.
why: 先 and 再 each sit directly before their own verb phrase, and the first action comes first. 先我 would copy English "first".

py: wǒ men xiān rè shēn zài bǐ sài
en: We will warm up first and then play the match.
why: 先 goes after the subject before 热身; 再 goes before 比赛. 再 cannot trail its verb.

zh: 我们先去公园放风筝，然后再回家吃饭。
py: wǒ men xiān qù gōng yuán fàng fēng zheng rán hòu zài huí jiā chī fàn
en: We will first go and fly kites in the park, and then go home to eat.
why: 然后 links the two steps and 再 still sits right before its verb phrase 回家吃饭. 先 stays after 我们.

zh: 妈妈先买菜，再做年夜饭。
py: mā ma xiān mǎi cài zài zuò nián yè fàn
en: Mum will buy groceries first and then cook the New Year's Eve dinner.
why: 先 then 再, each directly before its verb phrase and after the subject. Swapping the verbs would reverse the order of events.

task: Say that I run in the park too.
py: wǒ yě zài gōng yuán pǎo bù
en: I run in the park too.
why: 也 goes after the subject and before the verb phrase; it may also sit between 在公园 and 跑步, but never at the end.

src_py: wǒ men dōu xǐ huan pǎo bù

py: wǒ men dōu bù xǐ huan pǎo bù
en: None of us like running.
why: Negation comes after 都: 都不 means none. 不都 would only say that not all of us like it.

src_py: wǒ men kāi chē qù hǎi biān

py: wǒ men zuò huǒ chē qù hǎi biān
en: We go to the seaside by train.

src_py: wǒ men chī fàn rán hòu qù pá shān

en: We will eat first and then go hiking.

src_py: wǒ xià ge yuè qù huá xuě
task: Ask when you are going skiing.
py: nǐ shén me shí hou qù huá xuě
en: When are you going skiing?
why: The question word replaces 下个月 in its time slot before the verb. It is not moved to the end, and no 吗 is added.

src: 我昨天看了一场比赛。比赛很精彩。
src_py: wǒ zuó tiān kàn le yī chǎng bǐ sài bǐ sài hěn jīng cǎi
task: Join them into one sentence with 的.
zh: 我昨天看的比赛很精彩。
py: wǒ zuó tiān kàn de bǐ sài hěn jīng cǎi
en: The match I watched yesterday was great.
why: The first sentence becomes a modifier 我昨天看的 in front of 比赛, linked by 的. It cannot follow 比赛.

src_py: wǒ méi kàn guo nà chǎng qiú sài
task: Put the object first as the topic.
py: nà chǎng qiú sài wǒ méi kàn guo
en: I have not seen that game.
why: The known object moves to the front; the negation 没 still stays right before the verb after the subject.

src: 我想去划船，小王也想去。
src_py: wǒ xiǎng qù huá chuán xiǎo wáng yě xiǎng qù
task: Say you want to go with 小王.
zh: 我想跟小王一起去划船。
py: wǒ xiǎng gēn xiǎo wáng yī qǐ qù huá chuán
en: I want to go rowing with Xiao Wang.
why: The companion goes in the frame 跟…一起 before the verb, after the modal 想. 想去划船跟小王 is English order.

src_py: wǒ men zài lǎo jiā chī nián yè fàn
task: Add the time 除夕夜 (New Year's Eve night).
zh: 我们除夕夜在老家吃年夜饭。
py: wǒ men chú xī yè zài lǎo jiā chī nián yè fàn
en: On New Year's Eve we have the reunion dinner at our family home.
why: The time word is added before the place phrase, after the subject or ahead of it. Time precedes place.

src_py: bǐ sài shí diǎn kāi shǐ le
task: Say the match did not start until ten.
py: bǐ sài shí diǎn cái kāi shǐ
en: The match did not start until ten.
why: 才 (later than expected) follows the time word and precedes the verb, and the verb loses its 了.

zh: 他八点就到了，我十点才到。
py: tā bā diǎn jiù dào le wǒ shí diǎn cái dào
en: He was there as early as eight, but I did not arrive until ten.
why: 就 marks something earlier than expected, 才 something later. Swapped, eight would be late and ten early, which contradicts the cue.

q: 我们___喜欢滑冰，所以谁也不想去。
zh: 我们都不喜欢滑冰，所以谁也不想去。
py: wǒ men dōu bù xǐ huan huá bīng suǒ yǐ shéi yě bù xiǎng qù
en: None of us like skating, so nobody wants to go.
why: 都不 means none, which fits 谁也不想去. 不都 only means not all, so someone would still want to go; 不也 is not a possible order.

q: 我们___爱看球赛，有的人更喜欢游泳。
zh: 我们不都爱看球赛，有的人更喜欢游泳。
py: wǒ men bù dōu ài kàn qiú sài yǒu de rén gèng xǐ huan yóu yǒng
en: Not all of us love watching ball games; some prefer swimming.
why: 不都 means not all, matching "some prefer swimming". 都不 would say that none of us love watching them.

py: wǒ xǐ huan pá shān tā yě xǐ huan
en: I like hiking, and he likes it too.
why: 也 means "too" and sits before the verb. 再 and 又 mean "again" and do not fit a second person liking the same thing.

zh: 我们先去公园，再去吃饭。
py: wǒ men xiān qù gōng yuán zài qù chī fàn
en: We will go to the park first and then go and eat.
why: 先 marks the first step and 再 the second, each before its verb. 再 … 先 reverses the order, and 也 means "also", not "first".

py: tā yòng kuài zi chī jiǎo zi
en: He eats dumplings with chopsticks.
why: 用 + tool before the verb gives "with chopsticks". 跟 means "with a person" and 在 marks a place.

q: 我们___高铁去上海看灯会。
zh: 我们坐高铁去上海看灯会。
py: wǒ men zuò gāo tiě qù shàng hǎi kàn dēng huì
en: We take the high-speed train to Shanghai to see the lantern show.
why: 坐 is the verb for riding public transport, and it goes before 去. 骑 is for bikes and horses; 开 means to drive or operate it.

q: 过年时我___爷爷奶奶一起包饺子。
zh: 过年时我跟爷爷奶奶一起包饺子。
py: guò nián shí wǒ gēn yé ye nǎi nai yī qǐ bāo jiǎo zi
en: At New Year I make dumplings together with Grandpa and Grandma.
why: 跟 + person + 一起 is the frame for "together with". 在 would need a place and 给 means "for", so neither pairs with 一起.

q: 我想跟你___去看龙舟比赛。
zh: 我想跟你一起去看龙舟比赛。
py: wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ yī qǐ qù kàn lóng zhōu bǐ sài
en: I want to go and watch the dragon boat race with you.
why: The frame 跟…一起 puts the companion before the verb. 一直 (all along), 一定 (surely) and 一样 (the same) cannot complete it.

py: zhè shì wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de fēng zheng
en: This is the kite I bought yesterday.
why: The clause 我昨天买 describes 风筝, so it takes 的 before the noun. 了 would end the clause and 地 marks adverbs.

py: nǐ xiǎng wán shén me
en: What do you want to play?
why: The thing played is the object, so 什么 stays in the object slot after 玩. 哪儿 asks where and 谁 asks who.

py: nǐ shén me shí hou qù huá chuán
en: When are you going rowing?
why: 什么时候 is a time word, so it stands after the subject and before the verb. 怎么 asks how, and 哪儿 and 谁 do not fit this slot.

py: nǐ men zěn me guò duān wǔ jié
en: How do you celebrate the Dragon Boat Festival?
why: The cue asks how, so 怎么 goes before 过. 什么时候 would ask when and 哪儿 would ask where.

q: 我从小___喜欢踢球，现在还在踢。
zh: 我从小一直喜欢踢球，现在还在踢。
py: wǒ cóng xiǎo yī zhí xǐ huan tī qiú xiàn zài hái zài tī
en: I have always liked playing ball since I was little, and I still play.
why: 一直 means all along and fits 从小 … 现在. 一起 means together and 一定 means certainly, so neither fits the sense.

q: 我今天已经跑了五公里，明天___想跑。
zh: 我今天已经跑了五公里，明天还想跑。
py: wǒ jīn tiān yǐ jīng pǎo le wǔ gōng lǐ míng tiān hái xiǎng pǎo
en: I have already run five kilometres today, and I still want to run tomorrow.
why: 还 before the modal 想 expresses "still, in addition". 再 and 又 mean repeating an action and cannot sit before 想 here.

en: I run in the park.
why: The place phrase 在公园 must come before the verb. At the end it copies English "in the park".

why: A time-when word goes before the verb and can never close the sentence.

s: 我不想跟他一起去看比赛。
s_py: wǒ bù xiǎng gēn tā yī qǐ qù kàn bǐ sài
zh: 我不想跟他一起去看比赛。
py: wǒ bù xiǎng gēn tā yī qǐ qù kàn bǐ sài
en: I do not want to go to the match with him.
why: Correct: 不想 stands before the 跟…一起 frame, not between 一起 and the verb. This is the normal order.

s_py: tā chī màn màn de jiǎo zi
py: tā màn màn de chī jiǎo zi
en: He eats dumplings slowly.
why: The manner adverb 慢慢地 goes before the verb. After 吃 it would wrongly modify 饺子.

s_py: xiǎo wáng yòng shǒu jī kàn zú qiú sài
py: xiǎo wáng yòng shǒu jī kàn zú qiú sài
en: Xiao Wang watches the football match on his phone.
why: Correct: the tool 用手机 comes before the main verb 看, as in the usual means-before-verb pattern.

s_py: yě wǒ xǐ huan dǎ pīng pāng qiú
py: wǒ yě xǐ huan dǎ pīng pāng qiú
en: I like playing table tennis too.
why: 也 is an adverb and must follow the subject. It cannot open the sentence.

s_py: wǒ xǐ huan tī zú qiú yě
py: wǒ yě xǐ huan tī zú qiú
en: I like playing football too.
why: Chinese 也 never ends the sentence like English "too". It goes after the subject.

s_py: tā shí diǎn lái cái
py: tā shí diǎn cái lái
en: He did not come until ten.
why: 才 sits between the time word and the verb. It cannot follow the verb.

s_py: wǒ men dōu zài gōng yuán lǐ pǎo bù
py: wǒ men dōu zài gōng yuán lǐ pǎo bù
en: We all run in the park.
why: Correct: 都 comes right after the subject and before the 在 + place phrase. It does not go after the place.

s_py: wǒ men dōu yě xǐ huan yóu yǒng
py: wǒ men yě dōu xǐ huan yóu yǒng
en: We all like swimming too.
why: Stacked adverbs run 也 before 都. 都也 reverses them.

s: 他们都也没参加过比赛。
s_py: tā men dōu yě méi cān jiā guo bǐ sài
zh: 他们也都没参加过比赛。
py: tā men yě dōu méi cān jiā guo bǐ sài
en: None of them have entered the competition either.
why: The chain is 也, 都, 没. 都也没 puts 都 ahead of 也.

s: 我们都不会打网球，所以想请教练教我们。
s_py: wǒ men dōu bù huì dǎ wǎng qiú suǒ yǐ xiǎng qǐng jiào liàn jiāo wǒ men
zh: 我们都不会打网球，所以想请教练教我们。
py: wǒ men dōu bù huì dǎ wǎng qiú suǒ yǐ xiǎng qǐng jiào liàn jiāo wǒ men
en: None of us can play tennis, so we want to ask a coach to teach us.
why: Correct: 都不 means none of us, and 都 correctly comes before 不. The follow-up clause fits that reading.

s_py: tā men yě dōu méi qù guo hǎi biān
py: tā men yě dōu méi qù guo hǎi biān
en: None of them have been to the seaside either.
why: Correct: the chain 也, 都, 没 in the fixed order, with 没 closest to the verb.

s_py: wǒ kàn guo bǐ sài nǐ cān jiā de
py: wǒ kàn guo nǐ cān jiā de bǐ sài
en: I have seen the competition you took part in.
why: The clause 你参加的 must stand before the noun 比赛. A relative clause cannot follow its noun.

s: 我买了一双很贵的跑鞋。
s_py: wǒ mǎi le yī shuāng hěn guì de pǎo xié
zh: 我买了一双很贵的跑鞋。
py: wǒ mǎi le yī shuāng hěn guì de pǎo xié
en: I bought a pair of very expensive running shoes.
why: Correct: number and measure come first, then the description with 的, then the noun.

s_py: nǎ r nǐ qù dǎ qiú
py: nǐ qù nǎ r dǎ qiú
en: Where do you go to play ball?
why: 哪儿 stays in the slot where the answer would be. It is not moved to the front.

s_py: nǐ xiǎng kàn shén me bǐ sài ma
py: nǐ xiǎng kàn shén me bǐ sài
en: Which match do you want to watch?
why: A sentence with a question word already is a question, so 吗 must not be added.

s_py: shéi xiǎng gēn wǒ yī qǐ qù huá bīng
py: shéi xiǎng gēn wǒ yī qǐ qù huá bīng
en: Who wants to go skating with me?
why: Correct: 谁 opens the sentence only because it is the subject, in the very slot the answer would take.

s_py: zhè zhǒng yùn dòng wǒ yě méi shì guo
py: zhè zhǒng yùn dòng wǒ yě méi shì guo
en: I have not tried this kind of sport either.
why: Correct: the topic 这种运动 comes first and 也 still stays after the subject 我.

s_py: zhè ge yóu xì dōu wǒ men wán guo
py: zhè ge yóu xì wǒ men dōu wán guo
en: We have all played this game.
why: Even when the object is fronted, 都 stays after the subject 我们 and cannot precede it.

s: 先我们去划船，再去吃午饭。
s_py: xiān wǒ men qù huá chuán zài qù chī wǔ fàn
zh: 我们先去划船，再去吃午饭。
py: wǒ men xiān qù huá chuán zài qù chī wǔ fàn
en: We will go rowing first, then have lunch.
why: 先 is an adverb and follows the subject. It cannot open the sentence like English "first".

s: 我们再看龙舟比赛，先吃粽子。
s_py: wǒ men zài kàn lóng zhōu bǐ sài xiān chī zòng zi
zh: 我们先吃粽子，再看龙舟比赛。
py: wǒ men xiān chī zòng zi zài kàn lóng zhōu bǐ sài
en: We will eat rice dumplings first, then watch the dragon boat race.
why: The step done first takes 先 and the later one 再. Here the two are swapped, so the sequence is reversed.
